title: Check the type of common data types
description:
Write a function `type_names(*values)` that returns a tuple of the type name of each argument, using `type()`.

Continues Day 1's walkthrough script, which checks the type of one example each of: int, float, complex, string, list, and dict. Its last example, `{9.8, 3.14, 2.7}`, is commented '# Tuple' in the source - that comment is wrong; curly braces with no colons make it a set, and type() correctly reports 'set', which is what this exercise checks for too.
hints: type(value).__name__ gives the plain-text name of a value's type ('int', 'set', ...) rather than the full <class '...'> form.
Build a tuple of type(v).__name__ for each v in values - *values already collects every positional argument into one iterable to loop over.
expected_behavior: Returns the type name of each argument, in the order given.
solution:
def type_names(*values):
    return tuple(type(v).__name__ for v in values)
explanation: *values collects every positional argument into a single tuple inside the function, which a generator expression can then map over with type(v).__name__ - the same idea as Day 3's numeric_type_names, applied to a wider mix of built-in types.
